page: Amazon Web Services m6a.large is an entry-tier general-purpose virtual machine powered by the AWS Nitro System. It runs on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor clocked at 3.6 GHz. The instance is configured with one physical core providing two dedicated vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation is 8.0 GB of DDR4 running at 3 GHz, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Local NVMe instance storage is not included, and the instance operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-threaded performance alongside clear architectural limitations stemming from the two-thread footprint. The AMD EPYC architecture exhibits strong single-core compute performance in stress-ng tests and average results in single-threaded gzip compression and Geekbench single-core evaluations. However, aggregate multi-core throughput, including Geekbench multi-core and PassMark CPU metrics, falls into lower percentiles due to the single physical core constraint. Memory throughput also ranks on the lower end, recording 31.17 GB/s read and 21.04 GB/s write bandwidth on 256 MB uncached transfers.

The absence of integrated local storage necessitates network-attached Amazon EBS volumes for persistent storage, making internal I/O dependent on network allocations. Hardware encryption acceleration is supported via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets, though extended vector instructions like AVX-512 and AMX are not available.

Cost efficiency is driven by the use of AMD EPYC hardware, which generally offers a lower resource-cost profile than equivalent x86 alternatives for standard computing. The m6a.large is suitable for horizontal microservices, lightweight web serving, application backends, dev-test environments, and low-traffic enterprise utility tasks that do not demand extensive parallel execution.
description: Amazon Web Services m6a.large is a general-purpose virtual instance built on the AWS Nitro System, featuring an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.6 GHz. It provides two dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with multithreading, paired with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring remote Elastic Block Store volumes, and features a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations indicate respectable single-core computing and compression speeds, though aggregate multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics reflect the constraints of its two-thread envelope. Cryptographic hardware instructions like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI are supported, while advanced vector sets like AVX-512 are absent. Given its balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory configuration and cost-effective AMD architecture, m6a.large is well-suited for lightweight web services, containerized utility components, test environments, and non-intensive background operations.
